organizationsLists.description: Practicing cardiologist Dr. Shiv Rao founded Abridge in 2018 to free clinicians from the time-sucking paperwork that's required after they see patients: jotting down detailed notes for their medical records. Instead, Abridge records their conversations with patients and uses AI to both summarize them and fill out electronic health forms. Thousands of clinicians at health systems like John Hopkins Medicine and Mayo Clinic are already using it. In June 2025, the startup announced a $300 million Series E funding round supported by Andreessen Horowitz and Khosla Ventures, bringing its total funding to $830 million and bumping its valuation to $5.3 billion.

organizationsLists.description: Anthropic had a busy February. First Claude Cowork, designed to automate common business processes, spooked the market, sending SaaS, IT and legal services shares $285 billion lower. Then it launched its latest version of Claude Opus, its coding model that’s upending software engineering. Finally, it had a very public feud with the U.S. government. After refusing to budge on safeguards around autonomous weapons and mass domestic surveillance, Anthropic was blacklisted by the Pentagon. But that’s made CEO and cofounder Dario Amodei a hero of sorts in the AI world, with rivals like OpenAI and Google coming to his defense. And business keeps booming. Revenue hit $4.5 billion last year and in February Claude surpassed ChatGPT to become the most downloaded app on the App Store. It’s now valued at $380 billion.

organizationsLists.description: Former investment banker Grant Lee used to waste hours formatting text and designing graphics for PowerPoint presentations. Today, his startup Gamma lets anyone type in a simple text prompt to spin up sleek financial slides, visuals to go with social media posts and even entire websites. The app’s first version, launched in 2020, was a dud: one investor called it “the worst idea” they’d ever heard, Lee, 42, recalls. But the AI craze changed Gamma’s fortunes: It’s been profitable since 2023 and is now valued at $2.1 billion. One hundred million people have used its tools at least once and more than 600,000 are regular users, paying between $9 to $100 a month.

organizationsLists.name: AI 50
organizationsLists.description: Describe it, design it. That's how people use Midjourney's popular AI image generation tool, which is available via Discord and web app. CEO David Holz—a former NASA researcher who previously founded Leap Motion—started the San Francisco-based business in 2021. It has since been used to create everything from floral typography and watercolor-style art to realistic-looking images of Pope Francis or U.S. President Donald Trump, with the release of its V1 video model in June 2025. Midjourney—which brought in $300 million in total revenue in the 2024 fiscal year, according to PitchBook, and is profitable—has so far shunned any outside funding, but it did announce a technology licensing partnership with Meta in August 2025. Midjourney was also hit with a lawsuit in June 2025, with Disney and Universal suing for copyright infringement. In August 2025, Midjourney pushed back and argued fair use for AI model training, writing that “Copyright law does not confer absolute control over the use of copyrighted works.”

organizationsLists.name: AI 50
organizationsLists.description: Surge AI helps tech companies build smarter AI by supplying the human feedback that helps models understand nuance, like the difference between “this movie is the bomb!” and “this movie bombed.” The company works with customers such as Google, Meta and Microsoft, and has helped train models like Google’s Gemini and Anthropic’s Claude. Founder Edwin Chen was the youngest newcomer on this year’s Forbes annual ranking of the 400 richest Americans. He previously worked at Google, Facebook and Twitter, and told Forbes last year he wants Surge to encode the “richness of humanity.” That approach has fueled tremendous growth: In 2024, the company generated $1.2 billion in revenue and is now worth an estimated $24 billion, with talks underway to raise $1 billion at a $30 billion valuation, though no deal has closed yet.
